content:
*RESOLVED
–
 

1.  
That it be approved that the Council will take a lead role in
delivering the Tapton Terrace Project,
in partnership with the Environment Agency, to remove the risk to
life caused by flooding by acquiring and subsequently demolishing
the properties, subject to approval of an Outline Business Case
(OBC) by Government.
 

2.  
That it be noted that the OBC, which sets out the
details of the scheme, has been submitted to Government for
consideration and approval, which if approved, will fully fund the
project, with no requirement for funding to be provided by the
Council.
 

3.  
That authority be delegated, subject to approval of
the OBC, to the Director of Economic Growth, in consultation with
the Director of Governance and Director of Finance, to enter into
negotiations with landowners and residents to acquire properties
through private negotiation, and to conclude the necessary legal
processes in relation to the acquisition of the
properties.
 

4.  
That it be approved in principle that the use of Compulsory
Purchase Order (CPO) powers under Section 226(1)(b) of the Town and
Country Planning Act 1990 in the Council’s role as the Local
Planning Authority, or other such appropriate powers as may be
advised, if necessary and only as a last resort, to ensure that the
project can be delivered and risk to life mitigated.
 

5.  
That, alongside negotiations with affected parties,
the Council begin the preparatory work required to progress a CPO,
which would only be implemented as a last resort if consensual
agreement is not achievable after all reasonable efforts have been
made.
 
That it be recommended to Full Council;
 

6.  
That the addition of the Tapton Terrace
Project onto the capital programme be approved, and subject to
approval of the OBC, the approved capital and revenue funding be
added to the Council’s budgets.
 

7.  
That it be noted that the project will be fully funded by
Government grant funding, subject to the approval of the OBC.
 
REASONS FOR
DECISIONS
 

1.  
To endorse the Council taking a lead role in delivering the
project, to support the statutory authorities with responsibility
for water management and flood risk in Chesterfield, namely the EA
and DCC, to address the ongoing risk to life at Tapton Terrace and to prevent future deaths from
occurring, as outlined in the Coroner’s Prevention of Future
Deaths Report.
 

2.  
To authorise that the Director of Economic Growth
can enter into negotiations with affected landowners, occupiers and
other relevant interest holders to acquire by agreement,
all property interests through private
treaty, on a consensual basis, which is a direct negotiation
between a seller and a buyer.
 

3.  
To agree, in principle, the use of the
Council’s Compulsory Purchase powers, to support the delivery
of the scheme, as a last resort and only if absolutely necessary
and where acceptable terms cannot be agreed on a consensual basis,
to adequately prevent future deaths.
topline: The Council has decided to take a lead role in the Tapton Terrace Project to address the risk of flooding and prevent future deaths.

content:
The Director of Housing presented a report
seeking approval to reshape Housing Property Services (HPS) in
order to strengthen capacity, capability and resilience across the
service and support delivery of excellent services to council
tenants.
 
A major HPS transformation programme had been
underway since early 2024 and the structure and establishment of
HPS had not changed for several years with some job descriptions
over ten years old.
 
In recent years, and in anticipation of the
reshape, several posts in the original establishment had become
vacant and not filled, and there were various interim working
arrangements, secondments and agency-covered functions.
 
The key outcomes required from the reshape
were;
 
·       
Dedicated roles for people and performance management
·       
More flexibility and cooperation between teams to direct resources
to priority areas
·       
Dedicated resources for complaints and customer care
·       
Stronger financial management
·       
Job descriptions updated and re-evaluated to reflect new
requirements
 
The current structure for HPS was attached at
Appendix A to the officer’s report, and a proposed revised
structure was shown at Appendix B to the officer’s report.
The proposal had been developed following extensive consultation
and engagement with the team and trade unions, and to ensure the
required outcomes could be delivered.
 
The benefits of the proposed structure were
detailed at paragraph 4.16 of the officer’s
report.  Overall, the proposed structure
strengthened the service’s ability to deliver, better
outcomes for tenants, improved performance and responsiveness, and
stronger regulatory compliance and assurance.
 
*RESOLVED
–
 

1.  
That the proposed new structure and job descriptions for Housing
Property Services, as set out in Appendices B and C of the
officer’s report, be approved.
 

2.  
That the additional employee budget required to implement the new
structure, as set out in the financial implications section of the
officer’s report, be approved.
 

3.  
That the Director of Housing be authorised, in conjunction with the
Head of Housing Property Services, to implement the recommended
changes to the structure, roles and accountabilities of the
service.
 

4.  
That authority be delegated to the Director of Housing, in
consultation with the Director of Digital, HR and Customer
Services, the Director of Finance and the Cabinet Member for
Customers and Business Transformation, to make further minor
revisions to the structure and job descriptions if required,
subject to compliance with HR policies and procedures, and subject
to containment within the employee costs that have been set out in
the financial implications section of the officer’s
report.
 
REASON FOR
DECISIONS
 
To ensure the Housing Property Service has the
right capacity, leadership, technical capability and customer focus
to deliver safe, responsive and high-quality services to tenants,
support the Council’s regulatory improvement plan, and
progress the ambition to achieve a C1 consumer standard compliance
rating.
topline: The Joint Cabinet and Employment & General Committee has decided to approve recommendations for reshaping Housing Property Services to strengthen capacity and deliver excellent services to council tenants.

content:
The Director for Policy, Communications and
Local Government Reorganisation presented a report seeking approval
to reshape the Communications and Marketing service.
 
It was noted that the Communications and
Marketing service played a key role in the delivery of the
council’s strategic objectives and statutory duties, and was
a key enabling service that delivered the following support to the
Council and key partnerships;
 
·       
External communications and media relations for the Council and key
partnerships
·       
Internal communication and engagement
·       
Digital communications including website, intranet, and social
media
·       
Reputation management for the Council and key partnerships
·       
Marketing – Co-ordination and advice
·       
Emergency planning, business continuity and crisis
communications
 
All local authorities had faced a period of
financial challenges and increased demand leading to service
changes and redesigns, all of which required extensive
communication support. In addition, successive Government’s
had developed key funding streams for place regeneration and
community building which were led through extensive partnership
networks, such as Staveley Town Deal and United Kingdom Shared
Prosperity Fund.
 
Recent years had also brought a marked shift
in the media, communications and technology landscape. These
factors demanded a communications service that was more
risk?aware, agile and responsive than ever,
capable of navigating a complex environment while maintaining
public trust and confidence.
 
The current structure and establishment costs
were shown at Appendix A to the officer’s report.  An overview of the proposed changes and the
proposed new structure was also provided at Appendix B to the
officer’s report.
 
The new structure would release further
strategic capacity to support the critical Local Government
Reorganisation transition period and provide strategic advice for
senior leaders at Chesterfield Borough Council and within our
partnership’s spaces.
 
*RESOLVED
–
 

1.  
That the proposed new
structure of the Communications and Marketing service, as set out
in Appendix B of the officer’s report, be
approved.
 

2.  
That approval be granted to make minor amendments where necessary, to the small
number of job descriptions still under review, to ensure alignment
between the role requirements and evaluation outcomes. Final grades
to be determined by the established job evaluation panel in line
with the Council’s corporate scheme. The structure has been
costed at the highest potential grade, and the potential ranges
shown in the officer’s report.
 

3.  
That the Director
for Policy, Communications and Local Government
Reorganisation be authorised to implement the recommended changes
to the structure, roles and accountabilities of the Communications
and Marketing service.
 
REASON FOR
DECISIONS
 
To ensure that the Communications and Marketing service has
the strategic and operational capacity, capability and resilience
to meet forecasted workloads and priorities as set out in the
Council Plan 2026 – 2028 and supporting strategic plans. This
includes playing a central role in supporting the council’s
major change and transformation programme arising from Local Government
Reorganisation (LGR).
topline: The Joint Cabinet and Employment & General Committee has decided to approve a new structure for the Communications and Marketing service to support the council's strategic objectives and statutory duties.

content:
The Cabinet Member for Customers and Business
Transformation presented a report on the Review of the Careline
Service. In considering the matter, Members had regard to the
officer’s report and appendices, including the consultation
findings, the options appraisal and the Equality Impact
Assessment.
 
Members noted that Careline provided a 24/7
telecare monitoring and emergency falls response service supporting
older and disabled residents to live independently and safely in
their own homes, and that the decision therefore required careful
consideration of continuity of service, safeguarding and equality
impacts.
 
Members noted that, following Derbyshire
County Council’s withdrawal of funding for 24/7 falls
response provision in April 2024, the Council had continued to
deliver the service on the basis that it should achieve cost
neutrality. Despite efforts to retain and grow the customer base,
the service continued to operate at a deficit due to high fixed
costs and declining volumes.
 
Members noted that approval had been given on
24 February 2026 for public consultation on the review and that
consultation had taken place between 3 March 2026 and 22 April
2026. Members considered the 700 responses received, predominantly
from current service users and carers, together with the key themes
set out in the report and appendices, including concerns relating
to vulnerable residents, continuity of service, safety,
affordability and support for customers required to change
provider.
 
Members also noted that staff and recognised
Trade Unions had been consulted in parallel with the public
consultation and considered the key themes arising from that
process.
 
Members noted the evidence set out in the
report that two private sector organisations had indicated an
intention to provide telecare monitoring and 24/7 falls response
services within the borough, and that the availability of
alternative provision had been taken into account as part of the
Best Value assessment.
 
Members noted that shared service and
partnership options with neighbouring authorities had been explored
as alternatives to closure. Members considered the options
appraisal and noted the assessment that, having regard to
implementation complexity, timescales, customer-volume risk and the
uncertainty associated with Local Government Reorganisation, those
options were unlikely to provide a timely or sustainable Best Value
solution.
 
Members considered the Equality Impact
Assessment and had regard to the likely impact on older and
disabled residents together with the mitigating actions proposed,
including a managed transition, customer support, safeguarding
oversight and arrangements intended to maintain continuity of
service for those choosing to transfer to alternative provision.
Having considered the report and appendices in full, Members
accepted the officer recommendation that closure of the Careline
service, with a managed transition, was the option which best met
the Council’s Best Value duty in the circumstances.
 
*RESOLVED
–
 

1.  
That the closure of the Council’s Careline service from 1
August 2026, with a managed transition to support customers to move
to appropriate alternative telecare and 24/7 falls response
provision (where they choose to do so) ensuring there is no gap in
emergency response, be approved.
 

2.  
That authority be delegated to the Director of Digital, HR, and
Customer Services, in consultation with the Cabinet Member for
Customers and Business Transformation, to implement the closure
decision, including associated staffing implications, in accordance
with the Council’s HR policies and relevant employment
legislation.
 

3.  
That authority be delegated to the Director of
Digital, HR and Customer Services, in consultation with the
Director of Housing and the Cabinet Member for Customers and
Business Transformation, to procure an alternative provider for the
Council’s emergency out of hours telephone provision using a
compliant route and to put in place appropriate contract management
and performance arrangements to ensure a safe, resilient and value
for money service.
 

4.  
That authority be delegated to the Director of
Digital, HR and Customer Services, in consultation with the
Director of Housing and the Cabinet Member for Housing, to procure
an alternative alarm receiving centre (ARC) for the Council’s
independent living schemes through a compliant procurement route,
ensuring continuity of monitoring, appropriate safeguarding
assurance and robust contract management.
 
REASON FOR
DECISIONS
 
The review of the Careline service has
concluded that continued direct delivery will require significant
ongoing financial subsidy, placing additional pressure on the
Council’s ability to protect and invest in other priority
services for residents.  Having
considered the evidence, including the consultation findings, the
options appraisal and the Equality Impact Assessment, closure with
a managed transition is the option that meets the Council’s
Best Value duty while enabling mitigation to address potential
equality and safeguarding impacts.
topline: The Joint Cabinet and Employment & General Committee has decided to close the Council's Careline service with a managed transition to alternative providers.

duties on the Council to enforce a broader range of landlord
obligations.  To meet these

fully aligned with the new legislative framework.

in 2019 and now needs to be updated to reflect the new
requirements. The Council does not currently have a Civil Penalties
Policy and this is now necessary.

content:
The Cabinet Member for Customers and Business
Transformation presented a report seeking approval to reshape the
Human Resources (HR) and Payroll service.
 
The refreshed People Plan set
out the Council’s clear ambitions to support its employees
through the period 2026 to 2028, focusing not only on recruiting
and retaining great talent and developing staff for future roles,
but also on prioritising staff wellbeing to help employees thrive
during times of change. To successfully achieve these goals
the HR and Payroll service would need strengthening.  New roles had been built into the proposed
structure which would help support both strategic and operational
service delivery, enhancing learning and development provision,
improving the wellbeing initiatives which were available to staff,
and enabling the council to maintain high-quality transactional HR
services.
 
Table 1 at paragraph 4.5 of the
officer’s report set out the functional
activities which must be undertaken by the HR and Payroll service
over the next two years.  The
responsibilities relating to each of these functions were set out
in table 2 at paragraph 4.6 of the officer’s
report.
 
The proposed structure for the
HR and Payroll service, set out at Appendix B to the
officer’s report, had been designed to ensure the service was
optimally resourced to deliver the strategic ambitions set out in
the People Plan 2026 – 2028 alongside the day to day
operational activity required to support the council’s staff
to deliver council services and achieve the priorities set out in
the Council Plan for 2023 - 2028.
 
Implementation of the new
structure would be progressed in line with the Council’s HR
policies and procedures.  Trade Union
colleagues had been fully engaged in the development of the reshape
and were fully supportive of the proposals.
 
*RESOLVED
–
 

1.  
That the proposed new structure of the Human
Resources and Payroll service, as set out in paragraphs 4.7 to 4.9
and Appendix B of the officer’s report, be
approved.
 

2.  
That the new job descriptions and person
specifications for the roles as set out in Appendix C of the
officer’s report, be approved.
 

3.  
That £108,260 of additional funding be
allocated to the Human Resources and Payroll budget to meet the
increased employee costs of the new structure.  This would be met from the funding which was
approved by Full Council on 17 December 2025 to support
implementation of the People Plan 2026 – 2028.
 

4.  
That authority be delegated to the Director of
Digital, Human Resources and Customer Services, in conjunction with
the Head of Human Resources and Payroll, to implement the
recommended changes to the structure, roles and accountabilities of
the Human Resources and Payroll service.
 
REASON FOR
DECISIONS
 
To ensure that the Human
Resources and Payroll service is appropriately structured and made
up of officers with the right skills, knowledge and experience to
ensure the council has available to it an efficient, compliant and
engaged workforce whilst supporting the effective delivery of the
Council’s People Plan 2026 – 2028, and the vision,
priorities and objectives set out in the Council Plan 2023 –
2028.
topline: The Joint Cabinet and Employment & General Committee has decided to reshape the Human Resources and Payroll service to support employees and achieve strategic goals.

The Cabinet Member for Town Centres and
Visitor Economy presented a report seeking approval to restructure
Cultural Services to meet anticipated workloads, especially in
relation to the reopening of the Stephenson Memorial Hall, and to
strengthen the technical capabilities of the service.
 
Cultural Services was established in 2021,
bringing together the Arts and Venues service with the Tourism,
Museum, and Events service to create a unified service team. At
inception, the service comprised 70 staff members (approximately 32
full-time equivalents (FTE)), responsible for a range of council
venues including the Visitor Information Centre, Chesterfield
Museum, the Pomegranate Theatre, The Winding Wheel Theatre, Hasland
Village Hall, the Assembly Rooms, Revolution House, two Museum
stores, and five Rest Rooms.
 
The service had since evolved to meet changing
demands and by Summer 2025 staffing levels had been adjusted from
70 (32 FTE) to 58 (approximately 21.85 FTE) staff.
 
The current management and staffing structure
was set out at Appendix A to the officer’s report, and the
proposed structure, which would see the current establishment
increased by 7.40 FTE staff at Appendix B to the officer’s
report.
 
Appendix C to the
officer’s report set out the job descriptions for each of the
roles which were proposed in the new structure. These roles had
been through the Council’s job evaluation process, to
determine the grade and salary levels which should be
applied.
 
The staff had been consulted
for their views on the proposed structure and roles from 7 January
to 24 February 20206 and the Trade Unions also actively
engaged.
 
*RESOLVED
–
 

1.  
That the recommended staffing structure as described
in paragraphs 4.17 and 4.32 and illustrated at Appendix B of the
officer’s report be approved.
 

2.  
That authority be delegated to the Director of
Leisure, Culture and Community Wellbeing, working in conjunction
with the Cultural Services Manager and the Head of Human Resources
and Payroll, to implement the new Cultural Services staffing
structure, in line with the Council’s formal restructuring
policies.
 
REASON FOR
DECISIONS
 
By investing in the specialist skills,
customer experience, and operational roles which are highlighted in
the report, the service will be better equipped to handle growing
demand, ensure visitor satisfaction, and increase income. These
efforts will deliver long-term financial sustainability and help
Stephenson Memorial Hall and The Winding Wheel Theatre to become
leading cultural destinations offering significant value to the
community.
topline: The Joint Cabinet and Employment & General Committee has decided to approve the restructuring of Cultural Services to meet anticipated workloads and strengthen technical capabilities.

content:
The Cabinet Member for Climate Change,
Planning and the Environment presented a report setting out
information on natural burial, the proposal to develop a natural
burial site and the benefits to the local community and the
environment.
 
It was noted that 3,153 full burial plots
remained across the council’s four Cemeteries and 392
cremated remains plots. At current burial rates it was
estimated that around 40 years’ full burial space remained
within the Borough. Whilst it was noted that there was not an
immediate concern, this would need to be addressed at some time by
the responsible authorities if not now through the creation of a
natural burial site.
 
The creation of a Natural Burial Ground would
add approximately 1,500 full grave plots and 1,000 cremated remains
plots to the Cemetery Service’s capacity. At current burial
rates, the additional plots would add approximately 25 - 30 years
to the Borough’s existing burial capacity.
 
The feasibility of establishing a Natural
Burial Ground had been investigated over recent years, with
identification of an appropriate site taking some time to
establish. A privately owned piece of land to the south of
Brimington Cemetery had now been
identified, which would be a natural extension of the existing
Cemetery with good access and infrastructure already in place.
 
The full business case, attached at Appendix 1
to the officer’s report, set out the details of all
associated costs and projected income levels. The full
business case evidenced that the costs of land acquisition and of
development of the Natural Burial Ground, net of operating costs,
could be achieved within 15 years of operation.
 
*RESOLVED
–
 
1.   That the purchase and
development of land to the south of Brimington Cemetery, for the creation of a natural
burial site, subject to a successful planning application, be
approved.
 
2.   That authority be delegated to
the Director of Leisure, Culture and Community Wellbeing in
consultation with the Director of Economic Growth to negotiate the
details of a conditional contract and to enter into a conditional
contract to acquire the land from the landowner.
 
3.   That capital expenditure on
formulating conditional contracts and submitting a planning
application for the proposed use prior to acquiring the land be
authorised. This would include expenditure on the formulation of
such plans, proposals, surveys and studies as would be required to
support a planning application.
 
4.   That authority be delegated to
the Director of Leisure, Culture and Community Wellbeing in
consultation with the Director of Economic Growth to submit a
planning application to the Council’s Planning Committee for
the proposed use.
 
REASONS FOR
DECISIONS
 
1.   To offer the choice of an
increasingly popular funeral to the residents of the Borough and
improve the service offer of the Council’s bereavement
service.
 
2.   To add resilience to the
bereavement services’ facilities by increasing burial space
within the borough.
 
3.   To reduce the environmental
impact of funerals and burials on the environment, assisting the
Council in meeting its climate change commitments.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the purchase and development of land for a natural burial site to address limited burial space within the Borough.

content:
The Cabinet Member for Customers and Business
Transformation presented a report seeking approval
to commence a public consultation on the future of the Careline
service.
 
The review was necessary
because the service had been unable to attract sufficient customer
numbers to operate on a cost neutral basis.  The consultation would support evidence gathering
to inform sustainable options for future service
delivery.
 
The Careline service had
supported some of the borough’s most vulnerable residents for
many years, offering 24/7 telecare monitoring and falls response
services.  However, in 2024, Derbyshire
County Council (DCC) recommissioned its assistive technology and
falls recovery services, awarding the new countywide contract to
Medequip, while discontinuing a directly commissioned falls
recovery service.  This shift had
removed approximately £210,000 of annual contract income
previously used to support the Careline operating model. At that
time the Council had taken a decision to step in to protect the
service, with the ambition being to grow the customer base to make
the service cost neutral.
 
The service currently operated
at a deficit and now relied on temporary reserve support, including
the £300,000 Careline budget risk reserve established in
2024/25 to protect the General Fund from exposure while efforts
were made to achieve cost neutrality. 
Without a substantial increase in customer numbers the
service would not achieve cost neutrality and would continue to
exert financial pressure on the Council’s already limited
General Fund.
 
A comprehensive public
consultation was required to ensure that the views of residents,
service users, carers, partners and stakeholders could inform the
Council’s decision making.  The
proposed consultation would run for a period of eight weeks and
would use a blended multi-channel approach to maximise
accessibility.  In addition, formal
staff consultation would be undertaken with staff and trade unions
on the employment implications of potential changes.
 
Consultation outcomes would
directly inform the final options appraisal, risk analysis,
financial modelling and final Equality Impact Assessment, which
would be presented to Joint Cabinet and Employment & General
Committee for consideration.
 
*RESOLVED
–
 

1.  
That the commencement of an eight-week public
consultation on the future delivery model of the Careline service
be approved.
 

2.  
That authority be delegated to the Director of Digital, HR, and
Customer Services to begin an eight-week employee consultation
about how the Careline service could be provided in the future and
any possible effects on employment.
 

3.  
That authority be delegated to the Director of Digital, HR, and
Customer Services, in conjunction with the Cabinet
Member for Customers and Business Transformation, to implement a
temporary shared service arrangement with one (or more) Local
Authorities based within Derbyshire as set out in paragraph 6.5 of
the officer’s report.
 

4.  
That a further report setting out consultation
outcomes and options for the future of the service be
received.
 
REASON FOR
DECISIONS
 
Undertaking a public consultation is essential
to ensure that the views and experiences of service users,
potential customers, and other stakeholders are fully understood
before any decisions are made about the future of the Careline
service. Moreover, a transparent consultation process demonstrates
the Council's commitment to accountability and inclusivity in
shaping services that best meet local needs.
topline: The Joint Cabinet and Employment & General Committee has decided to commence a public consultation on the future delivery model of the Careline service.

content:
The Skills Delivery Manager presented a report
on behalf of the Leader of the Council which provided an update on
project proposals for the DRIIVe Rail Futures Project that would
support the delivery of training outputs at DRIIVe, and request
that funding to deliver the DRIIVe Rail Futures project that had
been made available to Chesterfield Borough Council from East
Midlands Mayoral Combined County Authority (EMCCA) was accepted and
that project activity could commence.
 
DRIIVe was being delivered in partnership by
Chesterfield Borough Council and Barrow Hill Ltd, with support from
the University of Derby who were collaborating in respect of
research and development activities. 
 
Funding for the construction of DRIIVe had
come from the Staveley Town Deal, the primary funder and
Chesterfield Borough Council.  In December 2024, Cabinet and
Council approved an additional internal funding contribution and
approved acceptance of external grant funding from EMCCA that
provided the remaining funding to deliver the capital element of
the project and allowed the Council to appoint a main contractor to
deliver the scheme.
 
DRIIVe received a further capital allocation
to contribute to the fit out of classroom facilities, in the final
UKSPF Investment plan that was approved by delegated decision on 25
March 2025.  The total capital costs of the project were
detailed in table 1 of the officer’s report.
 
In May 2025 an expression of interest for
funding was submitted to EMCCA seeking funding from the EMIZ
Flexible Fund to support the delivery of the Rail Futures Programme
at DRIIVe.  Funding had been provisionally allocated from the
EMIZ Flexible Fund to support delivery of the Rail Futures
Programme from January 2026 through until March 2029. Final
approval of the funding will be considered by the EMCCA Investment
Committee in April 2026.
 
It was proposed that the project would be
delivered in 3 phases: phase 1 and 2 within financial year 2025/26
and phase 3 across financial years 2026/2027, 2027/2028 and
2028/29.
 
Phase 1 would focus upon updating the training
requirement gap analysis that was undertaken as part of the 2019
feasibility study.  Phase 2 would make provision for the
contribution towards the base fit out of DRIIVe’s education
space, creating an environment that was fit for purpose and one
that would help attract a range of quality training providers for
the following procurement exercise.  Phase 3 would support the
procurement of a specialist training provider(s) that would deliver
training that responded to the training needs identified in the
refreshed training requirements gap analysis.
 
Key milestones for programme delivery were set
out in table 2 of the officer’s report.
 
*RESOLVED
–
 

1.  
That it be noted that funding from EMCCA of
£80,000 has been accepted under appropriate delegations to
deliver phases one and two of the DRIIVe Rail Futures
Project.
 
That it be recommended to Full Council:
 

2.  
That additional grant funding of £350,000 to
deliver phase 3 of the Rail Futures Project be accepted, subject to
external approvals from EMCCA.
 

3.  
That authority be delegated to the Director of
Economic Growth in consultation with the Cabinet Member for
Economic Growth, the Director of Finance and the Council’s
Head of Legal and Monitoring Officer to finalise the terms of grant
funding agreement in respect of phase three grant
funding.
 

4.  
That authority be delegated to the Director of
Economic Growth in consultation with the Cabinet Member for
Economic Growth and the Council’s Head of Legal and
Monitoring Officer to finalise procurement and contracting
arrangements in respect of the training provider
procurement.
 

5.  
That authority be delegated to the Director of
Economic Growth in consultation with the Cabinet Member for
Economic Growth and the Council’s Head of Legal and
Monitoring Officer to finalise contracting arrangementsand
depending on the contract option chosen, with the chosen training
provider and/orBarrow Hill Ltd in respect of delivery of the
scheduled outputs detailed in the Grant Funding
Agreement.
 

6.  
That a capital allocation of £20,000 be added
to the council’s capital programme in respect of the training
space fit out costs.
 
REASON FOR
DECISIONS
 
To secure funding to deliver
the Rail Futures project at DRIIVe which will support the
commitment made through the Staveley Town Deal to deliver
1680 days of training per year from DRIIVe, post building
completion.  The funding will also
provide an updated evidence base to ensure that the training
delivered optimises the opportunities in East Midlands Investment
Zone (EMIZ) priority sectors and meets the current needs of the
rail sector, accelerating the delivery of training
from DRIIVe.
topline: The Cabinet and Council have decided to accept funding for the DRIIVe Rail Futures Project, supporting training outputs and meeting the needs of the rail sector.

content:
The Cabinet Member for Town Centres and
Visitor Economy presented a report which provided a further update
on the progress in developing and delivering the comprehensive
renovation and refurbishment of Stephenson Memorial Hall, following
the report presented in October 2024.  An update on the action
plan, presented in the previous report, which established a pathway
to completion of the project, was also provided.
 
The delivery of a newly restored cultural
venue at Stephenson Memorial Hall was approved in December 2021, as
part of the Council’s successful Levelling Up Fund bid. Since
this time, the project had progressed through design development
and planning stages, with construction works commencing on site in
November 2023.
 
In October 2025, additional budget was
approved for specific extension of time requests granted to the
contractor, which revised the project budget.
 
The report set out a series of actions, to be
completed prior to bringing a further report back to Council, which
would aim to set out a full and final funding request to complete
the scheme.  These actions were detailed at paragraph 4.5 of
the officer’s report.
 
A full breakdown of the project budget was
last presented in December 2024, with an additional uplift agreed
in October 2025 which dealt specifically with two extensions of
time requests.  Issues that had led to the further additional
costs had been grouped under seven key headings for the summary set
out in Table 1 of the officer’s report.
 
The total budget uplift required, when
considering the movement in project cost, and the reinstatement of
a contingency, was demonstrated in Table 3 of the officer’s
report.
 
This was a significant increase in spend, but
the Council had been actively exploring routes for additional
external grant funding, to reduce the reliance on internal capital
contributions. Since October 2025, a significant grant of £1m
had been secured from the East Midlands Combined County Authority
(EMCCA) who had recognised the strong strategic alignment of the
Stephenson Memorial Hall project with their priorities for economic
growth and the visitor economy.
 
Confirmation had also been given by the Arts
Council that the existing grant funding could be deferred to the
2026/27 financial year.  Taking this into account, the
breakdown of funding required was shown in Table 4 of the
officer’s report.
 
*RESOLVED
–
 

1.  
That the current position regarding delivery of the Stephenson
Memorial Hall project be noted.
 
That it be recommended to Full Council:
 

2.  
That the revised budget for the delivery of the Stephenson Memorial
Hall refurbishment project, as outlined in Table 3 of the
officer’s report, be approved.
 

3.  
That the revised expenditure and financing arrangements for the
Stephenson Memorial Hall refurbishment project within the
Council’s capital programme, as summarised in Table 4 of the
officer’s report, be approved.
 

4.  
That grant funding from the East Midlands Combined County
Authority, as set out in Table 4 of the officer’s report, be
accepted to support the completion of the Stephenson Memorial Hall
project.
 
REASON FOR
DECISIONS
 
To ensure the delivery of a key
project within the approved Council Plan 2023-27, as well as an
objective of the Council’s Growth Strategy and Visitor
Economy Strategy.
topline: The Council has decided to approve a revised budget for the Stephenson Memorial Hall refurbishment project, including accepting grant funding from the East Midlands Combined County Authority.

content:
The Leader of the Council invited the Chief
Executive to present the report, which asked the Joint Cabinet and
Employment and General Committee to agree the process for the
appointment of a new Chief Executive following the decision of the
current postholder to retire in May 2026.
 
The report also proposed to
reset the shape of the Council’s Corporate Leadership Team to
ensure that it was appropriately structured and made up of senior
officers with the right skills, knowledge and experience to
continue to deliver the Council’s vision, priorities and
objectives whilst at the same time able to positively respond to
the substantial challenges and opportunities presented by local
government reorganisation (LGR).
 
The report also reviewed and
made recommendations on the levels of salary remuneration that
should be applied to individual roles within the Council’s
Corporate Leadership Team to ensure that the Council was able to
recruit the very best officers to its establishment and retain
their employment.
 
The current shape, roles and
individual accountabilities of the Council’s Corporate
Leadership Team (CLT) were set out in Appendix 3 to the
officer’s report. The report also detailed the
CLT’s current levels of performance and new challenges facing
and opportunities available to the CLT at sections 4.6 and
4.7.
 
The Chief Executive and the
Leader of the Council had spoken at length about the importance of
the role of Chief Executive and the options available to the
Council for filling the vacancy when it arose. To supplement
the process, it was proposed that an external technical assessor be
engaged. The assessor would typically be a practicing Chief
Executive or a recently retired Chief Executive with experience of
working at councils of a similar-size and make up to Chesterfield
Borough Council.
 
The final arrangements would be
agreed by the Leader of the Council and the Chair of the
Council’s Employment and General Committee but would
typically follow the stages detailed in section 4.20 of the
officer’s report.
 
It was recommended that the
2no. existing roles of Executive Director be replaced by a new role
of Deputy Chief Executive and that the roles and individual
accountabilities of the Service Directors remain largely
unchanged. There was however considered to be an urgent need
to increase capacity within the Service Director tier to
accommodate the significant additional burdens presented by
LGR.
 
The proposed future shape,
roles and individual accountabilities of the council’s CLT
were set out at Appendix 4 to the officer’s report, and to
support recruitment to the new roles of Deputy Chief Executive and
Service Director – Governance, new job descriptions and
person specifications had been developed. These were attached at
Appendices 5 and 7 to the officer’s report.
 
The proposals had been shared
with local Unison, GMB and Unite representatives. The Chief
Executive had considered the Trade Union representations, and his
responses were detailed in full at section 8.9 of the
officer’s report.
 
*RESOLVED
–
 
That the Joint
Cabinet and Employment and General Committee:
 

    
i.       
Notes the decision of the current Chief Executive to
retire on 6 May 2026.
 

   
ii.       
Agrees the process and timetable, as set out in
paragraphs 4.15 to 4.20 and Appendix 1 of the report, to recruit a
new Chief Executive with a view to the appointee starting their
employment on or before 6 May 2026.
 

 
iii.       
Approves the new job description and person
specification for the role of Chief Executive as set out in
Appendix 2 of the report.
 

 
iv.       
Agrees the new shape of the Council’s
Corporate Leadership Team and the proposed redistribution of
accountabilities and responsibilities between members of the
Council’s Corporate Leadership team, as documented in
paragraphs 4.21 to 4.31 and Appendix 4 of the
report.
 

  
v.       
Agrees that the role of Executive Director (2.0 FTE)
be deleted from the establishment and replaced by a new role of
Deputy Chief Executive (1.0 FTE).
 

 
vi.       
Approves the new job description and person
specification for the role of Deputy Chief Executive as set out in
Appendix 5 of the report.
 

 vii.       
Agrees that that the remaining holder of the role of
Executive Director be assimilated into the new role of Deputy Chief
Executive.
 

viii.       
Agrees that the role of Service Director –
Corporate be deleted from the establishment and replaced by a new
role of Service Director – Policy, Communications and Local
Government Reorganisation.
 

 
ix.       
Agrees that the role of Head of Regulatory Law and
Monitoring Officer be deleted from the establishment and replaced
by a new role of Service Director –
Governance.
 

  
x.       
Approves the new job descriptions for the roles of
Service Director – Policy, Communications and Local
Government Reorganisation and Service Director – Governance
as set out in Appendices 6 and 7 of the report.
 

 
xi.       
Agrees that the holder of the role of Service
Director – Corporate be assimilated into the new role of
Service Director – Policy, Communications and Local
Government Reorganisation.
 

 xii.       
Agrees that an external recruiter be appointed to
support the Council with the process of recruitment to the new role
of Service Director – Governance.
 

xiii.       
Notes the outcome of Gatenby Sanderson’s
salary benchmarking exercise, as documented in Appendix 8 of the
report, in relation to the roles of Chief Executive, Deputy Chief
Executive and Service Director.
 

xiv.       
Agrees the recommended levels of remuneration for
the roles of Chief Executive, Deputy Chief Executive and Service
Directors, as set out in paragraph 4.43 of the
report.
 

xv.       
Agrees that the roles of Service Director be
retitled Director for the reasons expressed in paragraph 8.6 i of
the report.
 

xvi.       
Agrees that the new structure and new levels of
remuneration be implemented from 1 December 2025.
 

xvii.       
Agress to reinvest the year-on-year savings
resulting from the Corporate Leadership Team reshape in workforce
learning and development with a particular emphasis on preparing
the Council’s workforce for the transition of their
employment from Chesterfield Borough Council to the new unitary
council for the Chesterfield borough area.
 

xviii.       
Authorises the Service Director – Digital,
Human Resources and Customer Services to update the Council’s
Senior Pay Policy Statement for 2025/26 to reflect the changes set
out within the report.
 

xix.       
Requests that the Council’s constitution be
updated to reflect the changes made to the Council’s
Corporate Leadership Team.
 

xx.       
Authorises the Chief Executive, in consultation with
the Service Director – Digital, Human Resources and Customer
Services and the Head of Human Resources and Payroll to implement
the recommended changes to the shape, structure, roles and
accountabilities of the Council’s Corporate Leadership
Team.
 
 
REASON FOR
DECISIONS
 
To ensure that
the Council’s Corporate Leadership Team is appropriately
structured and able to recruit and retain senior officers of the
right calibre and with the right skills, knowledge and experience

content:
*RESOLVED
–
 
That the Chesterfield Community
Safety Partnership Plan for 2025 – 2028 be noted and
endorsed.
 
REASONS FOR
DECISION
 

1.  
The Crime and Disorder Act 1998 placed a duty on the police and
local authorities to work together with key partners and
organisations to develop and implement local crime-reduction plans.
In doing so the Partnership must inform the plan based on local
need and analysis of crime and disorder levels and patterns in the
area and have regard to the objectives set out in the local Police
and Crime Plan.
 

2.  
The Chesterfield Community Safety Partnership (CSP) is responsible
for overseeing the development and implementation of an agreed
local Community Safety Partnership Plan. The partnership comprises
a wide range of organisations including Chesterfield Borough
Council (CBC), Derbyshire Constabulary, the Probation Service,
Derbyshire Fire and Rescue Service, Derbyshire County Council,
Public Health, plus a range of voluntary and community sector
organisations.
 

3.  
The CSP monitors and reviews the delivery and performance of
projects and interventions contained in the Chesterfield Community
Safety Plan. It considers performance and outcomes
while addressing gaps in service delivery and undertaking any
required statutory duties. The CSP also identifies, shares and
helps secure resources and funding to support the Chesterfield
Community Safety Plan.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to endorse the Chesterfield Community Safety Partnership Plan for 2025-2028.

*RESOLVED
–
 
That having given due consideration to matters
raised at Council on Wednesday 5 November 2025, Cabinet
resolved;
 

1.  
That the final proposal that has been developed for the
reorganisation of local government within the county area of
Derbyshire (as set out in Appendix B) be approved.
 

2.  
That option B (as described in paragraph 4.32 and Appendix 3 to
Appendix B) be adopted by Chesterfield Borough Council as the
‘base’ proposal for the reorganisation of local
government within the county area of Derbyshire.
 

3.  
That the Chief Executive, in consultation with the Leader of the
Council, be authorised to seek the Secretary of State for Housing,
Communities and Local Government’s approval to modify the
boundaries of the ‘base’ proposal for the reasons set
out in paragraphs 4.33 to 4,41.
 

4.  
That option B1 (as described in paragraphs 4.33 to 4.41 and
Appendix 3 to Appendix B) be adopted by Chesterfield Borough
Council as the basis for modifying the boundaries of the
‘base’ proposal for the reorganisation of local
government within the county area of Derbyshire.
 

5.  
That the Chief Executive, in consultation with the Leader of the
Council, be authorised to make any minor or technical amendments to
the final proposal prior to its submission to Government on or
before 28 November 2025.
 

6.  
That the Chief Executive, in consultation with the Leader of the
Council be authorised to submit the final proposal to the Secretary
of State for Housing, Communities and Local Government on or before
28 November 2025 and advise the Secretary of State of Chesterfield
Borough Council’s adopted options for the reorganisation of
local government within the county area of Derbyshire.
 
REASON FOR
DECISIONS
 
To enable Chesterfield Borough Council to
respond to Government’s formal invitation to councils in the
county area of Derbyshire (namely Derbyshire County Council, Derby
City Council and Derbyshire’s eight District and Borough
Councils) to make proposals for structural change, including the
creation of new unitary councils. Any proposals so developed are to
be submitted to the Secretary of State for Housing, Communities and
Local Government on or before 28 November 2025.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the final proposal for the reorganisation of local government in Derbyshire, with specific options adopted and modifications authorized.

The Cabinet Member for Town Centres and

comprehensive renovation and refurbishment of Stephenson Memorial
Hall. 
 
The report detailed the current status of the
project and presented recommendations for Cabinet and Council to
formally approve additional funding to meet contractual commitments
under the construction contract. The report also included a
detailed action plan to enable outstanding issues to be resolved,
and a further update report to be developed for Cabinet and Council
in December 2025.This report would set out a full and final capital
funding request, alongside a funding strategy, establishing a clear
pathway to project completion.
 
*RESOLVED
–
 
1.   That Cabinet note the current
position regarding delivery of the Stephenson Memorial Hall
project.
 
That it be recommended to Council:
 
2.   That the revised budget for the
delivery of the Stephenson Memorial Hall refurbishment project, as
outlined at Section 4.12 of this report, be approved.
 
3.   That the revised expenditure
and financing arrangements for the Stephenson Memorial Hall
refurbishment project within the Council’s Capital Programme
be approved.
 
REASONS FOR
DECISIONS
 
1.   To ensure the delivery of a key
project within the approved Council Plan 2023-27, as well as an
objective of the Council’s Growth Strategy and Visitor
Economy Strategy.
 
2.   To enable the Council to fulfil
additional contractual obligations in respect of the construction
contract.
topline: The Cabinet and Council have decided to approve additional funding for the renovation of Stephenson Memorial Hall.

content:
*RESOLVED
–
 

1.  
That the existing 22 Smoke Control Orders, as set
out in schedule 1 and 2 of Appendix A, which affect the
Council’s administrative area be revoked; and a single Smoke
Control Order covering the entire Borough as set out in the draft
order at Appendix B, be declared. Subject to confirmation by the
Secretary of State for Environment Food and Rural
Affairs.
 

2.  
That the Financial Penalties as set out in Appendix
D be approved and implemented. These penalties are introduced
pursuant to Section 19A and Schedule 1A of the Clean Air Act 1993,
which came into force on 1st May 2022 as a result of
amendments set out in Schedule 12 of the Environment Act
2021.
 

3.  
That the Smoke Enforcement Policy in Appendix C be
approved.
 

4.  
That authority be delegated to the Service Director
– Leisure, Culture and Community Wellbeing, in consultation
with the Cabinet Member for Health and Wellbeing, to make
amendments to the Smoke Enforcement Policy between the formal
review periods to enable operational effectiveness.
 
REASONS FOR
DECISIONS
 

1.  
To enable the Council to effectively and
proportionately enforce the powers under the Clean Air Act 1993 (as
amended by the Environment Act 2021 with effect from May 2022) for
dealing with smoke emissions in Smoke Control Areas
(SCAs).
 

2.  
To agree to the implementation and use of Fixed
Penalty Notices as an enforcement tool in connection with
smokey chimneys.
 

3.  
To ensure proper delegation and sub-delegation of
functions and powers.
 

4.     
To agree to the Smoke Enforcement Policy for the
investigation and enforcement of those new powers, including levels
of financial penalty to be imposed.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to revoke existing Smoke Control Orders, implement a single Smoke Control Order, approve Financial Penalties, and a Smoke Enforcement Policy.
